culture.title: Culture
culture.description: For each of the four core values — Humble, Hungry, Happy, Honest — here are the observable behaviors we can hire by, coach to, and reward. Use this in every 1-on-1 and quarterly review.
culture.howto_title: How to Use the Culture Guide
culture.howto_text: In every quarterly 1-on-1 and annual review, score each staff member on all four values using a 1-5 scale. A Right Person lives these values naturally. A Right Seat question is separate — someone can be a great fit to our culture but wrong for the role. Both matter.

values.name: Humble
values.description: Humility is the foundation. It's not thinking less of yourself — it's thinking of yourself less. We take Jesus seriously and not ourselves.
behaviors: Gives credit freely; takes blame personally
Asks for help without ego; actively seeks feedback
Serves outside their job description without complaint
Deflects praise toward the team and toward God
Listens more than they talk; curious, not defensive
Doesn't hoard information, decisions, or control

values.name: Hungry
values.description: Hungry people are self-motivated. They don't wait to be told. They pursue excellence in ministry because they love Jesus and love the mission.
behaviors: Pursues personal spiritual formation proactively
Reads, learns, and brings new ideas without being asked
Sets goals beyond what's required; moves the ball
Champions improvement and resists we've always done it this way
Takes on extra responsibility when the mission requires it
Execution-oriented — follows through without reminders

values.name: Happy
values.description: Happy doesn't mean always smiling. It means we know who we are in Christ, why we're here, and we find genuine joy in the work — even the hard parts.
behaviors: Brings energy to the team, not drama
Practices personal disciplines that sustain health (Sabbath, prayer, margin)
Celebrates wins — big and small — genuinely and publicly
Treats volunteers and guests with consistent warmth
Doesn't complain without offering a solution
Can receive hard feedback or news without falling apart

values.name: Honest
values.description: We say hard things with grace. No triangulating, no gossip, no sweeping things under the rug. Authenticity is not optional in this culture.
behaviors: Says what they mean in the room, not after the meeting
Admits mistakes quickly and owns outcomes fully
Brings problems forward — not sideways or backwards
Addresses conflict directly with the person involved
Keeps confidences; never leaks private matters
Doesn't shade truth to protect comfort or avoid awkwardness

ids.title: Issues List & IDS Process
ids.description: IDS — Identify, Discuss, Solve — is how you actually fix problems instead of talking around them forever. The Issues List is the shared, visible list of everything getting in the way.
ids.rule_text: Whoever identifies an issue owns putting it on the list — not solving it alone. The team solves it together in the L10. Issues are prioritized by impact, not urgency. An issue that recurs 3x becomes a Rock to fix systemically.

steps.label: Identify
steps.text: State the real issue, not the symptom. Sundays feel rushed means the issue is no documented run-of-show assigned. Be specific.

steps.label: Discuss
steps.text: Open the floor until the root issue is truly clear. Don't jump to solutions. Time-boxed to ~15 min/issue.

steps.label: Solve
steps.text: Create one To-Do: one owner, one due date. Issue is resolved or removed. Done.

culture_notes: Name personnel and pastoral issues clearly. Calling it tension doesn't solve it.
Issues belong to the team, not the person who raised them. No retaliation culture.
Never escalate to Ryan what Brad can solve. Never escalate to Brad what a director can solve.
IDS is not a venting session. Time-box discussion.
The Stepping Stones transition (post-Feb 2025) created systemic issues — these are Rocks, not just IDS items.
The Wonder gap means issues may not surface until they're critical. Build in explicit What are we missing? as a standing L10 prompt.
escalation: Issue appears in IDS for the 1st time — To-Do with owner + due date
Issue reappears for 2nd time — escalate priority; examine root cause
Issue appears for 3rd time — becomes a company Rock next quarter
Issues that involve Right Person / Right Seat — always escalate to Brad for private 1-on-1 follow-up
Building / facility issues — Ryan + Brad own together; surface at every QBOP
